title: Ambassador recruitment
summary: Move from a role brief to consistent assessment, approval, onboarding and programme review.
questions: Which region and communities?
What responsibilities and availability are needed?
Who approves selection and proposed terms?
steps: Agree responsibilities, region, availability and success measures.
Use relevant community referrals and opt-in outreach; record interest.
Use role-relevant criteria, the same questions and a small agreed sample.
Review proposed people, terms and support with the recorded approver before commitments.
Provide appropriate approved access, training, a first assignment and a support contact.
Check agreed outcomes, content quality and support needs; record improvements.

title: Discover and onboard artists
summary: Respect the artist's work and consent while moving from discovery to a complete, reviewed profile.
questions: Which craft, community or location?
Has the artist agreed to participate?
Which work, media and credits may be published?
steps: Describe the craft, region and fit; check the existing catalogue before adding a record.
Record reliable source links, reach out respectfully and confirm interest.
Explain intended use, credits and support; record consent and any restrictions.
Collect accurate biography, work details, image credits and permitted media.
Resolve missing facts and obtain the required consent and publication approval.
Agree a first opportunity, support contact and review date.

title: Events and workshops
summary: Plan purpose, contributors, venue, access, delivery and follow-up before making commitments.
questions: Who is it for and what is the outcome?
What access and practical support do attendees need?
Which dates, venue and quotes are confirmed?
steps: Confirm audience, purpose, format and success measures.
Compare venue suitability, contributor availability and practical requirements.
Assign delivery roles, agenda, equipment, access needs and contingency contacts.
Check quotes, agreements, cancellation arrangements and the required spending approval.
Provide clear date, location, registration and accessibility information.
Brief the team, support attendees, gather feedback and record outcomes.

title: Content and storytelling
summary: Develop source-grounded stories with contributor permissions, accessible formats and a clear review path.
questions: Who is the audience and what should they understand?
Which sources and contributors support the story?
Who approves publication?
steps: Agree audience, message, formats and success measures.
Verify facts and obtain contributor permissions, credits and restrictions.
Confirm people, assets, equipment and realistic availability.
Produce the story; check accuracy, captions, alt text and required formats.
Resolve review feedback and confirm the required publication approval.
Measure the agreed outcomes and use feedback to improve the next story.

title: Sales and customer follow-up
summary: Qualify needs, confirm a suitable offer, review terms and track outcomes without assuming a sale.
questions: Who is the intended customer?
What need and timing have they confirmed?
Who can approve pricing, availability and terms?
steps: Describe the product or experience, its value and the customers it can serve.
Confirm need, fit, availability and preferred next step; use only permitted contact information.
Check actual product availability, approved pricing, fulfilment needs and relevant terms.
Obtain the required approval; clarify questions and record the customer's actual decision.
Confirm the order or booking through its existing workflow and assign fulfilment responsibilities.
Record completed outcomes, feedback and the next follow-up; separate proposed from paid activity.

title: Partnership development
summary: Build a mutually useful partnership with explicit scope, reviewed commitments and measurable outcomes.
questions: What does each side gain?
Which contributions and deliverables are realistic?
Who reviews agreements and commitments?
steps: Agree audience, purpose, intended value and success measures.
Assess relevant organisations, fit and existing relationships before outreach.
Confirm interest, needs, contributions and practical constraints with the partner.
Define deliverables, responsibilities, proposed costs, timeline and measurement.
Use the recorded approver for agreements, spending and public claims before committing.
Coordinate work, check outcomes with both sides and agree improvements or renewal.

title: Business and revenue planning
summary: Separate the customer problem, proposed model, assumptions and evidence before scaling an idea.
questions: Which audience and problem?
What evidence supports the proposed value?
Which assumptions need validation and who reviews the plan?
steps: Describe the audience, problem, value proposition and existing evidence.
Document proposed offers, channels, operations and possible revenue streams as assumptions.
Review capacity, dependencies, available records and unknown costs; request quotes where needed.
Choose a bounded pilot with clear success measures, ownership and review points.
Check results, commitments and required approvals before investing or expanding.
Track the agreed measures, update assumptions and revise the next steps from evidence.

title: Community programmes
summary: Start with participant needs, clear expectations and a practical support and feedback loop.
questions: Which community and unmet need?
Who supports participants?
What participation and outcomes would count as success?
steps: Listen to participant needs and existing activity; define the purpose.
Explain expectations, accessibility, consent and how people can join or leave.
Assign facilitators, moderation, support contacts and a realistic activity cadence.
Check resources, permissions and required approvals before launching.
Invite relevant participants and collect feedback through the agreed channels.
Review meaningful participation, outcomes and support needs with the community.

title: Equipment and procurement
summary: Connect equipment to an actual need, compare viable options and obtain approval before purchase.
questions: What job must the equipment support?
Can existing equipment meet the need?
Which quote, training and approval are required?
steps: Describe the intended use, essential capabilities and the person responsible.
Review available equipment, borrowing and rental options before buying.
Collect current quotes and check compatibility, support and delivery constraints.
Submit the requirement, comparison and proposed cost through the existing approval workflow.
After approval, coordinate delivery, inventory, access and training.
Check whether the equipment meets the need and document maintenance and support.

title: Travel and artist visits
summary: Use actual dates, participant needs and quotes; treat budgets and arrangements as proposed until approved.
questions: What purpose and confirmed appointments?
Which travellers and dates?
Which arrangements, access needs and approvals remain open?
steps: Agree intended outcomes and the people or places to visit.
Confirm participant availability and appointment options before setting the itinerary.
List transport, accommodation, equipment and practical access needs; verify current requirements separately.
Use actual quotes and obtain the required approval before booking.
Confirm bookings after approval, contacts, schedule and a practical contingency plan.
Record outcomes, actual expenses and agreed follow-up.

title: Product and service experiments
summary: Validate a specific user need with a small experiment before treating an idea as proven.
questions: Which user need and evidence?
What is the smallest useful pilot?
Which result will change the next decision?
steps: State the user need, available evidence and the assumption to test.
Design a small useful offer or prototype with a bounded scope.
Agree success measures, feedback method, owner and review point.
Check resources, permissions and required approvals before starting.
Deliver the agreed experiment and collect permitted feedback.
Compare evidence with the success measures and choose to improve, stop or expand.

title: Training and team onboarding
summary: Make responsibilities, support and approved access clear, then check readiness through a practical first task.
questions: Which role and responsibilities?
What access is necessary and approved?
Who provides training and support?
steps: Agree responsibilities, required skills and what the first successful task looks like.
Choose role-specific guidance, practice and a support contact.
Use the existing access process and provide only what the role needs.
Complete a small supported task and resolve questions.
Review the outcome with the responsible person before independent work.
Schedule a check-in and update guidance from feedback.
